[[File:Museo Romano de Astorga.jpg|thumb|Facade of the Roman Museum, built over the so-called Roman Ergastula]]
[[File:Capilla de la Vera Cruz.jpg|thumb|Headquarters of the Confraternity of the Holy Vera Cruz and Confalón, home to the Holy Week Museum]]

=== Museums, archives, and libraries ===
The visual arts are represented in the Cathedral Museum, the Museum of Roads, and the Holy Week Museum. The Cathedral Museum, planned since 1889 by Bishop Grau, was inaugurated in April 1954 with two rooms under Bishop Jesús Mérida Pérez. Among its early visitors was the future [[Pope John XXIII]], and in 1989, [[Pope John Paul II]] visited while on the Camino de Santiago.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=126}}</ref> A 1982 renovation tripled the exhibition space by incorporating the former Cathedral School and Chapter House. It now occupies ten exhibition rooms across two floors, covering 1,400 square meters, housing liturgical and religious works from the cathedral.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Museo Catedralicio |url=http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/catedralicio.htm |access-date=8 November 2013 |publisher=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113070738/http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/catedralicio.htm |archive-date=13 November 2013}}</ref> The Museum of Roads is housed in the Episcopal Palace, reorganized as such in 1962 by Bishop Mérida Pérez, preserving the interior spatial layout. It displays artifacts from the diocese, related to the Camino de Santiago, which required proper storage due to abandonment or conservation needs. Across Gaudí's designed spaces—such as the dining room, official office, throne room, bedroom, chapel, and grand vestibule—are valuable artistic pieces, including Romanesque carvings and medieval [[goldsmithing]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Museo de los Caminos |url=http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/caminos.htm |access-date=17 December 2011 |publisher=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111218225728/http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/caminos.htm |archive-date=18 December 2011}}</ref> The basement showcases a collection of Roman and medieval archaeology and [[numismatics]], while the upper floor, designed by García Guereta, was adapted in 1975 to exhibit works by contemporary Leonese artists.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=91}}</ref>

While Holy Week imagery is stored independently in the city's parishes and the Episcopal Palace, the Confraternity of the Holy Vera Cruz and Confalón organizes a summer exhibition of its heritage, featuring notable pieces such as the Recumbent Christ, from the early 17th century by Gregorio Español; the Golden Cross, bearing the ''[[Lignum Crucis]]''; Jesus Tied to the Column and the Crucified, from the 16th century; and carvings from Levantine workshops.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Capilla Museo |url=https://www.santaveracruzyconfalon.com/ |access-date=30 September 2018 |publisher=Santa Vera Cruz y Confalón}}</ref> The Roman Museum, a historical museum, is located over the Roman structure known as the Ergastula. After the municipality fully acquired the building in 1996, it was renovated, adding two floors, and opened as a museum in 1999.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=57}}</ref> It exhibits artifacts from city excavations, illustrating the lifestyle of ancient Asturica Augusta from its origins to the late Roman period, forming a significant collection both quantitatively and qualitatively.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Museo Romano |url=http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/romano.htm |access-date=18 December 2011 |publisher=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094005/http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/romano.htm |archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

Dedicated to its chocolate industry, the city is home to the Chocolate Museum, founded in 1994 by José Luis López García and municipally owned since 2005. It displays objects from the city's 19th-century industrial phase, when the rise of muleteering spurred a nascent chocolate industry in the region. Its unique collection in Spain includes antique machinery, lithographic stones, engraving plates, and collections of chocolate trading cards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Museo del Chocolate |date=28 June 2016 |url=http://turismoastorga.es/museo-del-chocolate/ |access-date=30 September 2018 |publisher=Ayuntamiento de Astorga}}</ref> Since 2015, it has been housed in a new modernist mansion built by chocolatier Magín Rubio and designed by architect Eduardo Sánchez Eznarriaga.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Capital del chocolate |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/museo-chocolate-abre-etapa-busca-ser-referente-europa_957156.html |access-date=16 February 2015 |date=15 February 2015 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> Lastly, dedicated to the so-called "Astorga School", the Casa Panero was inaugurated in August 2011 as the home of the Panero family and a gathering place for [[Generation of '27]] members such as [[Gerardo Diego]] and [[Luis Rosales]], housing the works of the School's writers<ref>{{Cite news |title=La casa de la familia Panero abre en Astorga |url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2011/08/23/leon/1314097120.html |access-date=19 December 2011 |last=Sutil |first=Álvaro F. |date=24 August 2011 |newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=La Escuela de Astorga ya tiene su propio museo |url=http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2011/08/22/vivir/la-escuela-de-astorga-ya-tiene-su-propio-museo-125553.htm |access-date=19 December 2011 |last=Revuelta |first=Joaquín |newspaper=La Crónica de León |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111221181626/http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2011/08/22/vivir/la-escuela-de-astorga-ya-tiene-su-propio-museo-125553.htm |archive-date=21 December 2011}}</ref> and the legacy of archaeologist [[José María Luengo Martínez|José María Luengo]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=El legado de Luengo enriquece la Casa Panero |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/el-legado-de-luengo-enriquece-casa-panero_783440.html |last=López |first=Sara |date=2 April 2013 |access-date=25 June 2013 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

Astorga also has a municipal library, established in 1931 and reorganized in 1944, located in the former Hospice, a 19th-century building renovated in 1983 for cultural use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BM Astorga. Información |url=http://www.bibliotecaspublicas.es/astorga/informacion.htm |access-date=19 December 2011 |publisher=bibliotecaspublicas.es |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923184613/http://www.bibliotecaspublicas.es/astorga/informacion.htm |archive-date=23 September 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Additionally, the city is home to the municipal historical archive, with its oldest document dating to 1253, including one of Spain's two oldest council minutes, dated 27 December 1427,<ref>{{Cite news |title=Astorga conserva una de las dos actas municipales más antiguas de España |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/astorga-conserva-una-de-las-dos-actas-municipales-mas-antiguas-de-espana_527787.html |last=Almanza |first=Maite |date=15 May 2010 |access-date=19 December 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> and the Diocesan Archive, established in 1973, housing records from the diocese since 898.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Archivo Diocesano |url=http://www.diocesisastorga.es/node/105 |access-date=19 December 2011 |publisher=[[Diocese of Astorga]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120306205339/http://www.diocesisastorga.es/node/105 |archive-date=6 March 2012}}</ref>

=== Performing arts and bullfighting ===
[[File:Teatro Gullón.jpg|thumb|Facade of the Gullón Theatre]]
[[File:Golf & Folk.jpg|thumb|During the Saint Marta patronal festivities, the city hosts events such as street theater]]
Astorga is home to the Gullón Theatre, inaugurated in 1923. After its closure, it fell into disuse until the 1990s when it was converted into a nightclub. In 2006, the municipality purchased the building, and its restoration began in 2011;<ref>{{Cite news |title=El Ayuntamiento firma la compra del teatro Gullón y podrá acometer la rehabilitación |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/noticia.asp?pkid=243703 |date=17 January 2006 |access-date=24 December 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=El Teatro Gullón solo conservará las fachadas nobles |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/el-teatro-gullon-solo-conservara-las-fachadas-nobles_634139.html |last=Domingo |first=A |date=22 September 2011 |access-date=24 December 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> after several years of work, it reopened in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.astorgadigital.com/reformado-teatro-gullon-celebra-primera-jornada-puertas-abiertas/122936 |title=El reformado Teatro Gullón celebra su primera jornada de puertas abiertas |access-date=9 May 2020 |date=23 August 2017 |newspaper=Astorga Digital}}</ref> The city also has a cinema, originating as a theatre in 1911 and operating as a movie theatre since the 1930s.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Reabre el Cine Velasco |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/reabre-cine-velasco_779709.html |date=20 March 2013 |access-date=13 July 2013 |last=López |first=Sara |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

Several events related to performance and the arts take place in the city. During Carnival, a magic festival, held since 2004, brings together Spanish and international magicians.<ref>{{Cite news |title=La magia inundará Astorga por octavo año consecutivo |url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2011/02/23/leon/1298479206.html |last=Sutil |first=Álvaro F. |date=23 February 2011 |access-date=14 December 2011 |newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]}}</ref> In August, during the Santa Marta patronal festivities, the ''Ars Via'' street theatre festival features performances by various companies across the city over several days.<ref>{{Cite news |title=El teatro se abre paso en las plazas de Astorga |url=http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2009/08/28/vivir/el-teatro-se-abre-paso-en-las-plazas-de-astorga-47557.htm |last=Revuelta |first=J. |access-date=24 December 2011 |newspaper=La Crónica de León |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220024412/http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2009/08/28/vivir/el-teatro-se-abre-paso-en-las-plazas-de-astorga-47557.htm |archive-date=20 December 2013}}</ref> In September, since 1998, the Astorga Film Festival has been held,<ref>{{Cite web |title='El hombre que estaba allí' gana el primer premio del Festival de Cine de Astorga |url=http://www.ileon.com/cultura/032390/el-hombre-que-estaba-alli-gana-el-primer-premio-del-festival-de-cine-de-astorga |date=15 September 2013 |access-date=8 November 2013 |publisher=ileón.com}}</ref> featuring a national short film competition alongside activities such as film cycles, exhibitions, and conferences.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Festival |url=http://www.cineastorga.com/elfestival.html |access-date=16 December 2011 |publisher=Festival de Cine de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170923203321/http://www.cineastorga.com/elfestival.html |archive-date=23 September 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> During Christmas, since 2002, a story adapted for street theatre is performed across the historic center's streets.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Las calles se convierten en escenario de cuento |url=http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2009/12/28/comarcas/las-calles-se-convierten-en-escenario-de-cuento-62704.htm |access-date=24 December 2011 |newspaper=La Crónica de León |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131220021417/http://www.lacronicadeleon.es/2009/12/28/comarcas/las-calles-se-convierten-en-escenario-de-cuento-62704.htm |archive-date=20 December 2013}}</ref>

[[Bullfighting]] is not deeply rooted in Astorga, and the number of enthusiasts is relatively low, but it is common to schedule a bullfight during the Santa Marta festivities.<ref>{{Cite web |title=La Astorga taurina |url=http://www.astorga.com/articulo/toros.htm |access-date=July 13, 2013 |author=Isidro Martínez |website=Astorga.com}}</ref> The city has a [[bullring]] constructed in the early 20th century, partly using materials from the demolition of the Marquises' castle; prior to its construction, bullfighting events were held in the Plaza Mayor.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=72}}</ref> The most prominent figure in this field from the city is the bullfighter Julio Norte, who made his debut in the [[Íscar]] bullring in 1989.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Julio Norte |url=http://www.mundotoro.com/torero/julio-norte-espana/1289 |access-date=July 13, 2013 |author=Mundotoro.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150203182436/http://www.mundotoro.com/torero/julio-norte-espana/1289 |archive-date=February 3, 2015}}</ref>

=== Music ===
Music is a prominent element in the cultural life of the city, which has been home to musicians such as Juan de Oliver, composer of ''Sonatas de Palacio'', [[Evaristo Fernández Blanco]], a pioneer of [[serialism]] and composer of ''Obertura Dramática'', Venancio Blanco, who compiled ''Las mil y una canciones populares de la región leonesa'', Antonio Celada, and composers of sacred music such as José María Álvarez, Manuel Ansola, and González Barrón.<ref name="Alonso González 2000 185">{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=185}}</ref> Since the late 20th century, the organist Roberto Fresco has stood out.<ref name="ROB">{{Cite web |title=Curriculum |url=http://www.robertofresco.es/curriculum.html |access-date=November 19, 2013 |author=Roberto Fresco. Página oficial |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131028022024/http://robertofresco.es/curriculum.html |archive-date=October 28, 2013}}</ref>

The city is home to various musical groups, among which the municipal band, founded in 1894, stands out, though its origins date back at least to 1841.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historia |url=http://bandastorga.wordpress.com/historia/ |access-date=December 21, 2011 |author=Banda Municipal de Música |date=25 October 2008 }}</ref> Other ensembles represent a wide variety of musical styles, including choral, instrumental, Celtic, and rock, as well as the various bands that perform during Holy Week.

In July, the International Music Course, held annually since 1993, takes place and is considered a benchmark for music education in Castile and León, as it is the only one offering all orchestral and band specialties.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historia del CIM |url=http://www.cursomusicastorga.es/historia.html |access-date=July 18, 2013 |author=Curso Internacional de Música |archive-date=August 25, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130825142412/http://cursomusicastorga.es/historia.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> Also in the summer, the Music in the Cathedral series is held, featuring various sacred music concerts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tres virtuosos en el ciclo de Música de la Catedral |url=http://astorgaredaccion.com/not/1989/tres_virtuosos_en_el_ciclo_de_musica_de_la_catedral/ |access-date=July 18, 2013 |author=Astorga RedAcción |date=17 July 2013 }}</ref> Another musical event is the band competition, which offers a varied repertoire of processional marches each year in the days leading up to Holy Week.<ref>{{Cite news |title=El certamen de bandas de Semana Santa cumple 20 años |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/el-certamen-de-bandas-de-semana-santa-cumple-20-anos_774745.html |date=March 3, 2013 |access-date=June 25, 2013 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

=== Festivals and events ===
[[File:Zuiza.JPG|thumb|Zuiza Parade]]
[[File:Napoleónicos1.JPG|thumb|In April 2012, the bicentennial of the reconquest of Astorga by Spanish troops during the [[Spanish War of Independence]] was commemorated<ref>{{Cite news |title=Las calles de Astorga reviven la batalla que liberó a la ciudad del asedio francés en 1812 |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/las-calles-de-astorga-reviven-batalla-que-libero-a-ciudad-del-asedio-frances-en-1812_687284.html |access-date=May 16, 2012 |date=April 29, 2012 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>]]
Throughout the year, several cultural and festive events take place in the city. Chronologically, in mid-January, the Puerta de Rey parish celebrates the feast of Saint Anthony with the traditional procession and blessing of pets.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Aumentan las mascotas que acuden a la fiesta de san Antón |url=http://www.diariodeleon.com/noticias/astorga/aumentan-las-mascotas-que-acuden-a-fiesta-de-san-anton_579886.html |date=January 24, 2011 |access-date=December 14, 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> In February, the San Pedro de Rectivía parish honors [[Our Lady of Candelaria]] with a procession through the neighborhood.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los vecinos del barrio de Rectivía honran a la Virgen de las Candelas |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/los-vecinos-del-barrio-de-rectivia-honran-a-virgen-de-las-candelas_238161.html |access-date=December 14, 2011 |website=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> In the same month, on a movable date, Carnival festivities begin on Piñata Saturday, the first Saturday after Ash Wednesday, with a parade featuring over a hundred groups, bands, and floats;<ref>{{Cite news |title=El gran desfile de Astorga |url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2011/03/12/leon/1299970515.html |access-date=December 14, 2011 |date=March 13, 2011 |last=Sutil |first=Álvaro F. |newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]}}</ref> the weekend concludes with the burning of the Piñata on Sunday night.<ref name="FIE">{{Cite web |title=Fiestas |url=http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/fiestas/index.htm |access-date=December 14, 2011 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111214042749/http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/fiestas/index.htm |archive-date=December 14, 2011}}</ref> In mid-April, the feast of the patron saint Turibius is celebrated, complemented since the early 21st century with a trade fair and a [[tapas]] competition among the city's restaurants.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Un potaje para Santo Toribio |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/un-potaje-para-santo-toribio_602037.html |date=April 29, 2011 |access-date=December 15, 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> On a movable date, in years of drought, it is traditional to hold nine days of prayers in the cathedral to the Virgin of Castrotierra,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rubio Pérez |first=Laureano Manuel |year=1981 |title=La Virgen de Castrotierra. Su historia, santuario y romería |journal=Tierras de León: Revista de la Diputación Provincial |volume=21 |issue=42 |pages=75–88 |issn=0495-5773 |url=http://www.saber.es/web/biblioteca/libros/tierras-de-leon/html/42/7virgen.pdf |access-date=March 20, 2012 |archive-date=February 3, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120203135034/http://www.saber.es/web/biblioteca/libros/tierras-de-leon/html/42/7virgen.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> brought from her sanctuary seventeen kilometers away in a procession involving residents of nearby regions along with the [[pennon]]s of each locality, with the transfer decided by the vote of the Procurators of the Land.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=194}}</ref>

On a movable date, the Corpus Christi procession is held.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Numerosos fieles acompañaron a la Custodia |url=http://astorgaredaccion.com/not/1526/numerosos_fieles_acompanaron_a_la_custodia/ |access-date=July 10, 2013 |date=June 2, 2013 |newspaper=Astorga Redacción}}</ref> In June, every three years, the Zuiza festival is celebrated, an ancient commemoration of the Christian victory at the Battle of Clavijo, revived in 1994, during which the Clavijo Pennon—kept in the Town Hall—is processed, receiving honors as a captain general and escorted by fifty ''zuizones''.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Tradición ancestral |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/tradicion-ancestral_804491.html |last=López |first=Sara |date=June 17, 2013 |access-date=June 26, 2013 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> At the end of the same month, the San Andrés and San Pedro de Rectivía neighborhoods celebrate their festivals with traditional games and evening parties, among other events.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Comienzan las fiestas del barrio de San Andrés |url=http://astorgaredaccion.com/not/1740/comienzan_las_fiestas_del_barrio_de_san_andres/ |access-date=July 10, 2013 |author=Astorga RedAcción |date=20 June 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=El barrio de Rectivía celebra las fiestas de san Pedro |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/el-barrio-de-rectivia-celebra-las-fiestas-de-san-pedro_536507.html |access-date=July 10, 2013 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

At the end of July, the Astures and Romans Festival is celebrated, originating in 1986 and declared a Festival of Regional Tourist Interest in 2011;<ref name="TUREG">{{Cite web |title=ORDEN CYT/1429/2011, de 20 de octubre, por la que se declaran Fiestas de Interés Turístico de Castilla y León |url=http://bocyl.jcyl.es/boletines/2011/11/23/pdf/BOCYL-D-23112011-22.pdf |access-date=November 24, 2011 |author=Bocyl.es}}</ref> it commemorates the city's ancient past with events such as the Roman circus, Roman market, and the establishment of a Roman camp and Astur settlement in Melgar Park.<ref name="FIE" /> At the end of August, the city's patronal festivals in honor of Santa Marta take place, featuring evening parties, concerts, street theater, parades of giants and big heads, sports competitions, an artisan fair, and the traditional "Long Night", the highlight of the festivities with uninterrupted music until dawn.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|pp=197–198}}</ref><ref name="FIE" />

Finally, on movable dates—the first edition was in 2004—the Napoleonic Days are held, commemorating the events of the War of Independence, when the city endured two sieges by French troops.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Napoleón en Astorga |url=http://leonoticias.com/frontend/leonoticias/Napoleon-En-Astorga-vn21874-vst218 |access-date=January 27, 2009 |newspaper=Leonoticias.com}}</ref> The 2012 edition marked the bicentennial of the city's reconquest by General [[José María Santocildes|Santocildes]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=La crisis deja sin recreaciones a las Jornadas Napoleónicas de la ciudad |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/la-crisis-deja-sin-recreaciones-a-las-jornadas-napoleonicas-de-ciudad_546734.html |access-date=December 16, 2011 |website=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

=== Holy Week ===
[[File:Domingo de ramos astorga.jpg|thumb|Float of ''La Borriquilla'', processed on the morning of [[Palm Sunday]]]]
Holy Week in Astorga is declared a Festival of National Tourist Interest<ref name="TURNAC">{{Cite web |title=Resolución de 27 de julio de 2011, de la Secretaría General de Turismo y Comercio Interior, por la que se concede el título de «Fiesta de Interés Turístico Nacional» a la fiesta «Semana Santa» de Astorga (León). |url=http://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2011/08/09/pdfs/BOE-A-2011-13653.pdf |access-date=August 10, 2011 |author=boe.es}}</ref> and a Festival of Regional Tourist Interest,<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORDEN de 26 de septiembre de 1997, de la Consejería de Industria, Comercio y Turismo de la Junta de Castilla y León, por la que se declara Fiesta de Interés Turístico de Castilla y León |url=http://bocyl.jcyl.es/boletines/1997/10/28/pdf/BOCYL-D-28101997-2.pdf |access-date=February 13, 2011 |author=[[Junta de Castilla y León]]}}</ref> during which eight brotherhoods and confraternities, along with the Holy Week Promotion Board, process a total of forty floats.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Junta Profomento de la Semana Santa de Astorga |url=http://www.semanasanta-astorga.com/index.htm |access-date=January 1, 2009 |author=Junta Profomento |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112133133/http://www.semanasanta-astorga.com/index.htm |archive-date=January 12, 2012}}</ref> These eight include the Brotherhood of the Holy True Cross and Confalón, one of the oldest in the country, with its earliest document dating to 1475,<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=201}}</ref> the Royal Brotherhood of Our Father Jesus Nazarene and Most Holy Mary of Solitude, from 1674, the Archconfraternity of Our Lady of Sorrows, from 1911, the Brotherhood of the Knights of Silence of Our Father Jesus Nazarene, from 1926, the Brotherhood of the Blessed Christ of the Afflicted, from 1943, the Brotherhood of the Entry of Jesus into Jerusalem, from 1953, the Brotherhood of the Last Supper, from 1969, and the Brotherhood of the Ladies of the Virgin of Piety, from 1992.

Among the most notable events are the Way of the Cross, organized by the Holy Week Promotion Board and involving all brotherhoods; some of the events on Good Friday, such as the Encounter procession—with the traditional San Juanín race—, the Descent from the Cross in the Plaza Mayor, or the Solitude procession; and the Resurrection procession on Easter Sunday. Among the religious imagery, standout pieces include the Crucified Christ, from 1560, the Blessed Christ of the Afflicted, from the late 17th century, the Virgin of Solitude, also from the late 17th century, the Virgin of Sorrows, a 1706 work by José de Rozas, the Jesus Nazarene, from 1783, and the Golden Cross, from 1789. Alongside the religious aspects, various customs accompany the celebration during Holy Week, such as "[[Matar judíos|killing Jews]]" or eating ''bolla''—a pastry made of flour, honey, and milk—paired with [[muscat wine]].<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=204}}</ref>

=== Cultural life ===
Since the 19th century, Astorga has been a significant cultural center.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=179}}</ref> Among its earliest notable authors are Bishop [[Sampiro]], who between the 10th and 11th centuries wrote the ''Chronicle'' bearing his name, and Juan Lorenzo de Astorga, author, between the 13th and 14th centuries, of manuscript O of the ''[[Libro de Alexandre]]''.

The Church and its members played a prominent role in literary production; thus, figures emerged such as Alfonso de la Madre de Dios, with his 1618 work ''Chronica de la reforma de su religión'', Pedro Aingo de Ezpeleta, who published in 1634 ''Fundación de la Santa, Cathedral Iglesia de la ciudad de Astorga'', and Pedro Junco, who in 1639 published ''Fundación, armas y nombres de Astorga''. To these should be added the extensive documentary production generated by the diocese. In the 19th century, a range of authors gained prominence, including, among others, Marcelo Macías and Francisco Blanco García, author of ''Spanish Literature in the 19th Century'', both from the ecclesiastical sphere, jurists such as Alfonso de Villadiego, Mateo Martínez Moreda, Manuel García Prieto, and Manuel Prieto de Castro, and the bibliographer Andrés Martínez Salazar.

At the beginning of the 20th century, the wealth generated by the chocolate industry fostered the emergence of a prosperous bourgeoisie, among whose descendants a true "cultural Parnassus" was born, with poets such as [[Juan Panero]] and [[Leopoldo Panero]], literary critics such as [[Ricardo Gullón]], and writers such as Luis Alonso Luengo, all part of the so-called "Astorga School".<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=182}}</ref> In the following years, this cultural splendor was enriched by other poets such as Eugenio de Nora and Esteban Carro Celada, novelists such as José María Goy, intellectuals such as Julio Carro, and scholars such as Augusto Quintana Prieto, Eduardo Aragón, and [[José María Luengo Martínez|José María Luengo]], as well as literary gatherings and debates held in various city venues such as the Café Moderno, Café Iris, and Gran Café Universal. Additionally, several theatrical societies were established, affiliated with the Casino, the Catholic Circle, the Segura cultural center, La Unión, and the Friendship Society.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=183}}</ref>

Since the last decades of the 20th century, the city's cultural life has been driven not only by the various events held but, especially, by the more than fifty associations that exist, which organize numerous cultural activities and events throughout the year.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=192}}</ref> These include social, cultural, sports, parents', and neighborhood associations.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.detalle/idpag.64/relcategoria.370/idmenu.1050/chk.022cf67a1a10fa252817377e4fa81684.html |title=Asociaciones de Astorga |access-date=November 8, 2013 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704062558/http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.detalle/idpag.64/relcategoria.370/idmenu.1050/chk.022cf67a1a10fa252817377e4fa81684.html |archive-date=July 4, 2013}}</ref>

=== Language ===
{{See also|Leonese language}}
{{Blockquote|"Pastorcicus semus, d'Uriente venimus, bulsillus trayemus, diñeiro pidimus. Que Dios vus lo dea para nus lu dar. L'astrella nus guia a este santu hogar."<br>''Shepherds' song for Epiphany.''<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso Garrote|2011|p=97}}</ref>}}
[[File:Ríu Xerga.JPG|thumb|Protest graffiti advocating for the use of traditional toponymy on road signs<ref>{{Cite book|last=González Arias|first=Ismael María|title=L'Asturies cismontana|year=2003|isbn=978-84-95640-67-3|location=|publisher=Publicaciones Ámbitu|page=124}}</ref>]]
The language spoken in the municipality is Spanish or Castilian, but until the 20th century, numerous forms derived from Leonese, belonging to the western variant of [[Asturleonese]], persisted in everyday speech in Astorga and its surroundings, as well as in [[Maragatería]].<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso Garrote|2011|p=22}}</ref> Phonetically, some of the main features included the diphthongization of /o/ and /e/, the preservation of falling diphthongs, the inflection of the tonic vowel, the substitution of final /o/ with /u/, and the retention of the initial Latin /f-/. In terms of morphology, notable features included a scarcity of prefixes and, conversely, an abundance of suffixes, especially diminutives, and regarding its verbal system, the absence of compound tenses and the placement of personal pronouns after the verb.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso Garrote|2011|pp=27–85}}</ref>

In recent years, various groups such as La Caleya and Faceira have undertaken efforts to defend and promote the Leonese linguistic heritage through activities such as organizing Leonese language courses, informative talks, and literary competitions.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/la-caleya-entrega-los-premios-del-concurso-de-relatos-en-leones_376060.html |title=La Caleya entrega los premios del concurso de relatos en leonés |access-date=December 19, 2011 |date=March 25, 2008 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]] |archive-date=March 19, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319132229/http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/la-caleya-entrega-los-premios-del-concurso-de-relatos-en-leones_376060.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/cultura/xose-anton-gonzalez-riano-cierra-hoy-con-una-charla-los-cursos-de-leones-organizados-por-caleya_393117.html |title=Xosé Antón González Riaño cierra hoy con una charla los cursos de leonés organizados por La Caleya |access-date=December 19, 2011 |date=June 25, 2008 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]] |archive-date=March 20, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320081947/http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/cultura/xose-anton-gonzalez-riano-cierra-hoy-con-una-charla-los-cursos-de-leones-organizados-por-caleya_393117.html |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://astorgaredaccion.com/not/2150/concurso_literario_en_la_lengua_de_nuestros_abuelos/ |title=Concurso literario en la lengua de nuestros abuelos |access-date=August 2, 2013 |newspaper=Astorga Redacción}}</ref> In collaboration with the Culture Department of the Junta of Castile and León, the Provincial Council of León—through the Leonese Institute of Culture—and the Astorga City Council, several traditional Leonese story competitions were held, involving schoolchildren up to 14 years old from the province of León; the stories, written in the linguistic variants of León—Leonese, Galician, and Castilian—were compiled in the book ''Cuentos populares leoneses (escritos por niños)''.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/cultura/caleya-organiza-concurso-cuento-leones_61732.html |title=La Caleya organiza el concurso de cuento leonés |access-date=September 30, 2018 |date=January 18, 2003 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> Likewise, as a result of the collaboration between the cultural associations Facendera pola Llengua and La Caleya, in 2009, ''El Prencipicu'' was published,<ref>{{Cite book |author=Antoine De Saint-Exupéry |title=El Prencipicu (traducción del ''Principito'' al cabreirés por varios autores) |year=2009 |publisher=El Búho Viajero |isbn=978-84-96872-03-5}}</ref> a version in the Cabreirés dialect of the work by French writer [[Antoine de Saint-Exupéry]], ''[[The Little Prince]]''. The book emerged from pedagogical work with seven Cabreira students at the Astorga IES student residence within the so-called Cabreira Culture Classroom.

=== Traditional clothing ===
[[File:Maragato des environs d'Astorga.jpg|thumb|Illustration of a ''maragato'' from the mid-19th century]]
[[File:Murias, maragatos.jpg|thumb|Group of ''maragatos'' from Murias de Rechivaldo]]
An important part of ''[[Maragato]]'' folklore is its traditional clothing. The typical [[muleteer]] outfit, used during the 18th, 19th, and early 20th centuries, is notable among traditional attire for its continued daily use until a relatively late date; it is categorized as an occupational outfit, worn during travel, and is characterized by its functionality, with materials and shapes that protected against the elements and facilitated muleteer activities, evolving little over time, making it distinctly different from the clothing of other Leonese ''comarcas'', unlike women's clothing, which progressively lost variety and distinctiveness.<ref name="TRA">{{Cite web |title=Traje maragato |url=http://museodeltraje.mcu.es/popups/01-2009.pdf |access-date=December 16, 2011 |author=[[Museo del Traje]]}}</ref>

The men's outfit consisted of a shirt, vest, waistcoat, breeches or trousers, a belt—embroidered for festive days and dancing, according to social status—[[gaiters]], shoes, a hat, and a cape. Some of these garments, such as the waistcoat or breeches, appear to date back to the 16th or 17th centuries, according to various authors;<ref name="TRA"/> the latter are somewhat unique compared to those used in other Spanish ''comarcas'', being wide or baggy breeches, finding similarity only in the traditional attire of [[Mallorca]].<ref name="MARA">{{Cite book |last=Sutil Pérez |first=José Manuel |year=1997 |title=Maragatos en un desfile |page=22 |location=León |publisher=Ediciones Leonesas |isbn=84-8012-165-3 }}</ref>

The {{Interlanguage link|Women's clothing in Spain|lt=women's outfit|es|Indumentaria femenina en España}} is an evolution of the ancient attire, influenced by the clothing of neighboring areas and lacking the originality of the men's attire, but it retains great richness in terms of garments and accessories. It consists of a white skirt, a ''zagalejo'' (in cloth of various colors, depending on the wearer's social status), a ''faltriquera''—an inner pocket—a ''manteo'', an apron—embroidered in silk or felt, depending on social status—a [[Doublet (clothing)|doublet]], a neck scarf, a headscarf—different for single and married women—a mantle for religious ceremonies, ribbons and white lace, shoes, and jewelry—[[earrings]] or chokers, pendants, and rings. An exception to this typology is the outfit of the [[May Queen]]s, young dancers, which is more vibrant and colorful than the traditional ''Maragato'' attire, featuring red, green, and white prominently.<ref name="MARA"/>

=== Crossroads of paths ===
Due to its location and historical development, Astorga has been a meeting and departure point for paths, peoples, and cultures since ancient times.<ref name="Alonso González 2000 17"/> During the [[Ancient Rome|Roman period]], it was connected to the main cities of the time through several [[Roman road|communication routes]]. In the so-called ''Astorga Tablets'' from the 3rd century,<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/cultura/los-analisis-resuelven-enigma-de-las-tablas-de-barro-de-astorga-son-autenticas_783372.html |title=Los análisis resuelven el enigma de las Tablas de barro de Astorga: son auténticas |access-date=June 26, 2013 |last=Viñas |first=Verónica |date=April 2, 2013 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=García y Bellido |first=A. |year=1975 |title=El llamado "Itinerario de barro" |journal=Boletín de la Real Academia de la Historia |volume=172 |issue=3 |pages=547–563 |url=http://descargas.cervantesvirtual.com/servlet/SirveObras/35772718989144619754491/013781.pdf?incr=1 |access-date=May 16, 2012 |archive-date=August 30, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050830232432/http://descargas.cervantesvirtual.com/servlet/SirveObras/35772718989144619754491/013781.pdf?incr=1 |url-status=dead}}</ref> various routes mentioning Asturica are cited. Also in the 3rd century, the ''[[Antonine Itinerary]]'' indicates the network of communications linking the city with [[Bracara Augusta]] ([[Braga]]) via route XVIII, or through Lucus Augusti ([[Lugo]]) on route XIX, to [[Augusta Emerita]] ([[Mérida (Spain)|Mérida]]), to [[Tarragona]] via [[Caesaraugusta]] ([[Zaragoza]]) on route XXXII or Ab Asturica Terracone, or with [[Bordeaux]], via route XXXIV or [[Ab Asturica Burdigalam]]: practically to the four cardinal points of [[Hispania Tarraconensis]], through which troops, travelers, and products, mainly gold from [[Las Médulas]], were transported.<ref group='note'>Asturica became a communications hub in western Hispania, as recorded in the ''[[Antonine Itinerary]]'', compiled during the reign of Emperor [[Caracalla]] (211 to 217 CE).</ref>

From the south, the so-called Silver Route connected Mérida with Astorga (''Iter ab Emeritam Asturica'') and centuries later coincided in parts with the Cañada Real de la Vizana, along which [[transhumance|transhumant]] herds traveled from Extremadura to the Leonese mountains.<ref group='note'>This route was used by the Arabs to penetrate the northern peninsula. They named it B'lata, meaning "well-paved road."</ref> In modern times, it forms part of one of the main communication routes structuring western Spain, from Gijón to Seville, via the N-630 and the [[Autovía A-66|Silver Route motorway/highway]]; various institutions promote this axis as a tourist route called the Silver Route,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rutadelaplata.com/ |title=Ruta Vía de la Plata |access-date=April 19, 2012 |author=Red de Cooperación de Ciudades en la Ruta de la Plata}}</ref> which has generated controversy, as historical evidence defines its route exclusively between Mérida and Astorga, and the Association of Silver Route Towns, chaired by the Astorga mayor's office, has carried out protest actions since 2006 against the artificial extension of the Route.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.abc.es/20081010/castilla-leon-castilla-leon/astorga-boicotea-acto-promocional-20081010.html |title=Astorga boicotea un acto promocional en Barcelona de la "falsa" Vía de la Plata |access-date=April 19, 2012 |date=October 10, 2008 |newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/noticia.asp?pkid=449700 |title=Los pueblos de la vía apelarán a la Junta para que señalice la calzada |access-date=April 19, 2012 |date=April 26, 2009 |last=Almanza |first=Maite |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

To the east, the road connecting Asturica with Legio, which then continued to Caesaraugusta, was used as the Camino de Santiago and became the basis for the current [[N-120 road (Spain)|N-120]]. To the west, the road to Lucus Augusti and [[Gallaecia]] also became, centuries later, a section of the Camino de Santiago, which, leaving Astorga, passes through Foncebadón, Ponferrada, and Villafranca del Bierzo, among other places.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=19}}</ref> Around these main routes, other paths were woven, such as those used by muleteers or for [[Razzia (military)|razzias]], utilized by [[Tariq ibn Ziyad|Tariq]], [[Musa ibn Nusayr|Musa]], or [[Almanzor]], as well as by French troops during the Spanish War of Independence. All these routes were always active, contributing to the exchange of people and cultures and the introduction of various artistic styles. Currently, Astorga preserves the history of some of these communication routes in the Museum of the Paths, established in 1962.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Museo de los Caminos |url=http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/caminos.htm |access-date=May 21, 2012 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120621065756/http://www.ayuntamientodeastorga.com/quevisitar/caminos.htm |archive-date=June 21, 2012}}</ref>

;Camino de Santiago
[[File:Albergue de peregrinos de Astorga.jpg|thumb|Exterior view of the Siervas de María pilgrim hostel]]
Of the various pilgrimage routes to Santiago de Compostela, the most widely used and well-known since the Middle Ages is the French Way, which originated from the Roman road [[Ab Asturica Burdigalam]]. Its route reaches Astorga from the town of [[San Justo de la Vega]], entering the city through the former Sun Gate, which no longer exists. The pilgrim continues through San Francisco (formerly Calle de las Tiendas), Plaza Mayor, Pío Gullón (previously Rúa Nueva), Santiago Crespo, Santiago (formerly Caleya Yerma), and arrives in front of the Episcopal Palace, the Church of Santa Marta, and the cathedral. From there, the pilgrim proceeds through Leopoldo Panero, San Pedro, reaching the modern San Pedro Church in the Rectivía suburb. Crossing the [[N-6 road (Spain)|N-6]], the path continues toward the Foncebadón Pass.

During the Middle Ages, the city had numerous hostels or hospitals for pilgrims. Some, such as the Hospital of San Juan Bautista, where according to tradition [[Francis of Assisi|Saint Francis]] spent a few days recovering, gave rise to modern charitable institutions, but most disappeared over the centuries, leaving only their memory and some descriptions in preserved documentation. Until the late 1980s, pilgrims found shelter and lodging through the [[Catholic religious congregation|congregation]] of the [[Brothers of Our Lady of Lourdes]],<ref>{{Cite book |last=Valiña Sampedro |first=Elías |year=1985 |title=El Camino de Santiago, guía del peregrino |url=https://archive.org/details/elcaminodesantia0000vali |page=[https://archive.org/details/elcaminodesantia0000vali/page/116 116] |publisher=Everest |isbn=84-241-4200-4 |access-date=May 22, 2012}}</ref> but since then, these services have been provided, on one hand, by the Association of Friends of the Camino de Santiago in Astorga,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amigos del Camino de Santiago de Astorga |url=http://www.caminodesantiagoastorga.com/ |access-date=May 22, 2012 |author=Asociación de Amigos del Camino de Santiago}}</ref> which, after operating in various locations, has managed the Siervas de María hostel since 2006, with a total of 164 beds, and on the other hand, by the San Javier hostel, opened in 2003 and managed by the Vía de la Plata Cultural Association, offering 110 beds, and the Só Por Hoje hostel, opened in 2019, offering 10 beds.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.alberguescaminosantiago.com/poblaciones/astorga-leon-camino-de-santiago/ |title=Astorga, León, Camino Francés :: Guía del Camino de Santiago |access-date=June 2, 2022 |website=Albergues del Camino de Santiago |language=es}}</ref> The Association of Friends received the Elías Valiña Award in 2007 from the [[Government of Galicia]], recognizing its efforts in promoting the Jacobean routes.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asociación de Amigos del Camino de Santiago |url=http://www.caminodesantiagoastorga.com/index.php?modulo=1&noticia=42 |access-date=May 22, 2012 |author=Asociación de Amigos del Camino de Santiago}}</ref>

=== Gastronomy ===
[[File:Cecina.jpg|thumb|Plate of ''[[cecina de León]]'']]
[[File:Mantecadas de Astorga.jpg|thumb|''[[Mantecadas de Astorga]]'']]
[[File:Merles de Astorga.jpg|thumb|''Merles de Astorga'']]
{{See also|Leonese cuisine}}

Astorga's gastronomy is tied to the region's agriculture and livestock. The most famous dish is the Maragato stew, characterized by being served in reverse order, starting with the meats—which can include up to twelve types—followed by chickpeas, potatoes, and vegetables, then the soup, and ending with dessert, typically custard.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cocido Maragato |url=http://www.castrillodelospolvazares.net/cocido_maragato |access-date=January 1, 2014 |author=www.castrillodelospolvazares.net |archive-date=February 24, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200224011640/http://www.castrillodelospolvazares.net/cocido_maragato |url-status=dead}}</ref> The reason for this reversed order is not definitively known, but the custom seems to originate with the [[muleteer]]s, who preferred to eat cold meat first and then heat the soup upon arriving in a town.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=210}}</ref>

Other notable dishes include garlic soup, muleteer-style conger eel, sweetbreads in sauce, cabbage with cod, and ''[[cecina de León]]'', a cured beef product that has held a [[Geographical indication|Protected Geographical Indication]] since 1994, with its Regulatory Council based in Astorga.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Página oficial |url=http://www.cecinadeleon.org/ |access-date=September 30, 2010 |author=Consejo Regulador de la Cecina de León}}</ref> These culinary options, fundamental to the region's people, are preserved and promoted by the Gastronomic and Cultural Association "El Borrallo", whose cooking days culminate in the [[pig slaughter]], yielding various products.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Las jornadas de cocina de El Borrallo alcanzan su ecuador con la matanza |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/noticia.asp?pkid=108329 |access-date=September 30, 2010 |last=Almanza |first=Maite |date=November 17, 2003 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

In terms of confectionery, sweets hold a prominent place in Astorga's cuisine. The most famous are the ''[[Mantecadas de Astorga]]'', which have a Protected Geographical Indication.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mantecadas de Astorga |url=http://www.mantecadasdeastorga.es/igp.html |access-date=January 3, 2009 |author=IGP Mantecadas de Astorga |archive-date=September 21, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170921064423/http://www.mantecadasdeastorga.es/igp.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> The first written mention of them dates to 1805, and their commercialization began in 1850; their origin is uncertain, though it is believed the recipe came from a nun at the Sancti Spiritus convent who left the order to marry and popularized it.<ref>{{Harvnb|Alonso González|2000|p=211}}</ref> Another sweet, also widespread in the province, is the [[Hojaldres|''Hojaldres de Astorga'']], puff pastries soaked in syrup, originating in the mid-20th century.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hojaldres de Astorga |url=http://www.patrimonio-gastronomico.com/panreposteria_c.shtml?idboletin=129&idseccion=415&idarticulo=3251 |access-date=January 3, 2009 |author=patrimonio-gastronomico.com}}</ref> Also notable are the ''merles'', a puff pastry filled with cream and topped with caramelized sugar,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asemac |url=http://www.asemac.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=265&Itemid=123 |access-date=January 3, 2009 |author=Asemac}}</ref> and chocolate, present in Astorga since the mid-19th century, when the city had 41 chocolate factories in 1916, of which only four remain.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Alonso|first=Joaquín|title=Astorga. Ciudad Bimilenaria|year=2000|isbn=84-8183-073-9|location=León|publisher=Ámbito|page=212}}</ref>

== Media ==
[[File:El Faro Astorgano.jpg|thumb|Headquarters of the newspaper ''El Faro Astorgano'']]
;Print media
Astorga's journalistic tradition dates back to 1852, when the first periodical, the ''Boletín Eclesiástico del Obispado'', was published. By the end of the century, in 1885, the weekly ''Pedro Mato'' appeared, in 1892, the Catholic weekly ''La Luz de Astorga'', and in 1899, ''El Heraldo Astorgano''. In 1903, ''La Lid'' was published three times a week under the motto "freedom, progress, morality, and work", and ''El Faro Astorgano'', a Catholic newspaper, was founded. The following year, ''El Pensamiento Astorgano'' began publication, in 1906, ''El Evangelio en Astorga'', and in 1907, ''El Adalid''. Later, in 1917, the weekly ''El Fresco'' was born, and in 1928, the weekly ''Humo'' began under the guidance of Ricardo Gullón, Leopoldo Panero, and Luis Alonso Luengo.<ref name="Alonso González 2000 185"/>

Of these, ''El Faro Astorgano'' is the most prominent, with regional, provincial, and autonomous reach, available in both print and digital editions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Faro Astorgano |url=http://www.astorga.com/faro/ |access-date=April 11, 2012}}</ref> It is joined by the ''Cuadernos Municipales'', dedicated to historical and artistic heritage, the magazine ''Catedral'', by the Friends of the Cathedral association, the magazine ''Argutorio'', by the Monte Irago cultural association, and publications by several Holy Week brotherhoods. Major national newspapers, as well as the provincial ''[[Diario de León]]'' and ''La Nueva Crónica'', are also available.

;Electronic media
In Astorga, listeners can tune in to national and regional radio stations, as well as local stations that broadcast programs dedicated to local news at different times of the day. Examples include [[Cadena COPE|COPE Astorga]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ricardo García y Cristina Fernández: responsables de COPE Astorga |url=http://adelantobanezano.com/?interview=ricardo-garcia-y-cristina-fernandez-responsables-de-cope-astorga |access-date=June 9, 2013 |work=El Adelanto Bañezano |date=May 21, 2012}}</ref> and Castilla y León Radio.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://guiadelaradio.com/emisoras-leon |title=Emisoras León – Guia de la Radio |access-date=October 9, 2021 |language=es}}</ref>

Regarding digital media, at the local and regional level, notable are the two websites of the City Council, offering significant institutional and tourist information, the digital version of ''El Faro Astorgano'', the digital newspaper ''Astorga Redacción'', founded in 2013,<ref>{{Cite news |title='Astorga Redacción', un nuevo digital conducido por Antonia Reinares |url=http://tamtampress.es/2013/03/08/astorga-redaccion-nuevo-digital-conducido-por-antonia-reinares/ |access-date=June 9, 2013 |date=March 8, 2013 |newspaper=tamtampress.es}}</ref> the digital newspaper ''Diario de Astorga'', founded in 2014,<ref>{{Cite news |title=La sociedad astorgana tiende la mano al nuevo Diario de Astorga |url=http://www.astorgadigital.com/la-sociedad-astorgana-tiende-la-mano-al-nuevo-diario-de-astorga/39863 |date=March 21, 2014 |access-date=February 8, 2016 |newspaper=Diario de Astorga}}</ref> and the portal Astorga.com.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Astorga.com |url=http://www.astorga.com |access-date=April 18, 2012}}</ref>

== Sports ==
[[File:Fachada La Eragudina.jpg|thumb|Facade of the La Eragudina sports complex, where [[Atlético Astorga FC|Atlético Astorga]] plays its matches]]
;Sports entities
The most important sports entity in the city is the [[Atlético Astorga FC|Atlético Astorga Club de Fútbol]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlético Astorga C.F. |url=http://www.atleticoastorga.com |access-date=April 18, 2012}}</ref> which competes in the [[Tercera División|Spanish Third Division]]. [[Futsal]] has a strong tradition in the city, which until 2001 was home to the [[Astorga FS|Astorga Fútbol Sala]] team, which played in the [[Primera División de Futsal|First Division]] of the [[LNFS|Spanish Futsal League]] from its founding in 1989 until 2001, when the club dissolved due to financial difficulties.<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Dulma Astorga desaparece |url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD03/PUB/2001/02/20/EMD20010220021MDP.pdf |access-date=April 18, 2012 |newspaper=[[El Mundo Deportivo]]}}</ref>

Other sports or activities practiced in Astorga include cycling, with the Astorga Cycling Club, [[slot car racing]], with the Slot Club Astorga, motor sports with the Moto-Quad Senderos Maragatos sports club or the Astorga Motorcycle Sports Club, hiking with the La Salle sports club, and [[kung fu]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asociaciones deportivas |url=http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.detalle/idpag.81/cat.380/chk.dfce95d37cd38c935128ff2e62a2c62a.html |access-date=November 8, 2013 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130705161425/http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.detalle/idpag.81/cat.380/chk.dfce95d37cd38c935128ff2e62a2c62a.html |archive-date=July 5, 2013}}</ref> at the school run by the Jiménez family, known for their displays of strength and endurance.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nuevos retos para los Jiménez |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/nuevos-retos-para-los-jimenez_626633.html |access-date=April 18, 2012 |date=August 20, 2011 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Los Jiménez, una familia de forzudos |url=http://www.antena3.com/noticias/sociedad/jimenez-familia-forzudos_2010082600166.html |access-date=April 18, 2012 |author=((Antena3.com))}}</ref> Additionally, the City Council operates various municipal sports schools for athletics, basketball, futsal, Leonese wrestling, and swimming.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Escuelas Deportivas Municipales |url=http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.listado/relcategoria.382/relcategoriainicial.371/idmenu.116/chk.f6135cbf3c1be67133cc1fc70f1007a2.html |access-date=November 8, 2013 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704062508/http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.listado/relcategoria.382/relcategoriainicial.371/idmenu.116/chk.f6135cbf3c1be67133cc1fc70f1007a2.html |archive-date=July 4, 2013}}</ref>

;Sports events
Among the main sports events organized in the city are, on one hand, the Cycling Tour Against Drugs, which annually gathers several hundred participants for a route around Astorga,<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/provincia/mil-seiscientos-contra-droga_559604.html |title=Mil seiscientos contra la droga |access-date=April 18, 2012 |date=October 18, 2010 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> and on the other hand, local tournaments in various disciplines such as football, billiards, or tennis during the patronal festivals of Santa Marta at the end of August.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/astorga/las-fiestas-patronales-contaran-con-un-presupuesto-de-330-000-euros_211868.html |title=Las fiestas patronales contarán con un presupuesto de {{formatnum:330000}} euros |access-date=April 18, 2012 |last=Merino |first=Silvia |date=August 12, 2005 |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref>

In 1947, 1967, and 2011, Astorga was a stage start or finish for the [[Vuelta a España]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/salida.asp?n=Astorga |title=Salidas y Metas. Astorga |access-date=April 18, 2012 |author=lavuelta.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102193049/http://historia.lavuelta.com/es/salida.asp?n=Astorga |archive-date=January 2, 2014}}</ref> and it has also been a passage point several times for the [[Vuelta a Castilla y León]] and the [[Vuelta Ciclista a León]].

;Facilities
For sports practice, there are various facilities located mainly in the La Eragudina area: the football field "La Eragudina", where Atlético Astorga plays its matches,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.terrenosdejuego.com/detalle-campo.asp?Id_Team=1059 |title=La Eragudina |access-date=April 18, 2012 |author=terrenosdejuego.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102192607/http://www.terrenosdejuego.com/detalle-campo.asp?Id_Team=1059 |archive-date=January 2, 2014}}</ref> the Felipe Miñambres Municipal Sports Pavilion, municipal swimming pools, a gymnasium, several tennis courts, and two [[padel]] courts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.listado/relcategoria.381/relcategoriainicial.371/idmenu.116/chk.4605967ac2c76a1062f57410e738e3e7.html |title=Instalaciones Deportivas Municipales |access-date=November 8, 2013 |author=Ayuntamiento de Astorga |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704062512/http://www.aytoastorga.es/index.php/mod.pags/mem.listado/relcategoria.381/relcategoriainicial.371/idmenu.116/chk.4605967ac2c76a1062f57410e738e3e7.html |archive-date=July 4, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.diariodeleon.es/noticias/noticia.asp?pkid=499758 |title=La zona deportiva de Astorga incluye pistas de pádel y una piscina de recreo |access-date=April 18, 2012 |date=January 5, 2010 |last=Domingo |first=A. |newspaper=[[Diario de León]]}}</ref> Additionally, Astorga has a motocross circuit located in the El Sierro area.

WIKIPEDIA ARTICLE: Biogas
======================================================================

{{short description|Gases produced by decomposing organic matter}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2020}}
[[File:Biogas_plant.svg|thumb|270x270px|Simple sketch of household biogas plant]]
{{Sustainable energy}}
'''Biogas''' is a renewable gaseous fuel generated from organic materials including agricultural residues, manure, municipal waste, plant matter, sewage, wastewater, green waste, and food waste. Biogas is produced industrially via [[anaerobic digestion]] with [[Anaerobic organism|anaerobic organisms]] or [[Methanogen|methanogens]] inside an anaerobic digester or other type of [[bioreactor]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.simgas.com/advantages-of-biogas/how-does-biogas-work/item46|title=How does biogas work?|last=Webdesign|first=Insyde|website=www.simgas.com|language=en|access-date=2018-05-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180510115131/http://www.simgas.com/advantages-of-biogas/how-does-biogas-work/item46|archive-date=10 May 2018}}</ref> The gas composition is primarily methane ({{chem|CH|4}}) and carbon dioxide ({{chem|CO|2}}) with small amounts of [[hydrogen sulfide]] ({{chem|H|2|S}}) produced as a byproduct. Biogas is typically saturated with [[Water vapor|water vapour]] as a result of anaerobic micro-organisms living in water. Trace quantities of [[Volatile organic compound|volatile organic compounds]] and [[Siloxane|siloxanes]] can also vapourize into biogas, if they are present in the biomass feedstock.

Biogas is considered to be a [[renewable energy]] resource as the methane can be combusted to release energy. This energy release allows biogas to be used as a [[fuel]]. Biogas and its derivatives are used for multiple purposes including heat for cooking, electricity generation, and as a vehicle fuel.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=http://www.clarke-energy.com/gas-type/biogas/ |title=Biogas & Engines|publisher=clarke-energy.com|access-date=21 November 2011}}</ref> At a high level, biogas is a [[carbon-neutral fuel]] in so far as emissions of carbon dioxide from its combustion are matched by carbon dioxide pulled from the atmosphere to produce biomass.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-29 |title=Are Biofuels Carbon Neutral? Feedstocks & Applications |url=https://farmonaut.com/blogs/are-biofuels-carbon-neutral-feedstocks-applications |access-date=2025-10-20 |language=en-GB}}</ref> In practice, the carbon intensity of biogas can vary depending on emissions from the production of biomass and the processes used to produce and upgrade biogas.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Government of Canada |first=Canada Energy Regulator |date=2023-11-24 |title=CER – Market Snapshot: Two Decades of Growth in Renewable Natural Gas in Canada |url=https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/data-analysis/energy-markets/market-snapshots/2023/market-snapshot-two-decades-growth-renewable-natural-gas-canada.html |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=www.cer-rec.gc.ca}}</ref> In some applications, the capturing of biogas can avoid emissions of methane reducing overall emissions.<ref>Liebetrau, J., Ammenberg, J., Gustafsson, M., Pelkmans, L., Murphy, J.D. (2022). The role ofbiogas and biomethane in pathway to net zero. Murphy, J.D (Ed.) IEA Bioenergy Task 37, 2022</ref>

Biogas can be [[Biogas upgrader|upgraded]] to [[natural gas]] quality specifications by stripping carbon dioxide and other contaminants. Biogas that has been upgraded to interchangeability with natural gas is called [[renewable natural gas]] (RNG). RNG can be used as a drop-in fuel in the gas grid or to produce [[compressed natural gas]] as a vehicle fuel.<ref name=":0" />
{{TOC limit|3}}

==Production==
Biogas is produced by microorganisms, such as [[methanogens]] and [[sulfate-reducing bacteria]], performing anaerobic respiration. Biogas can refer to gas produced naturally and industrially.

As of 2026, biogas production primarily comes from large-scale industrial plants.<ref name=":12" />{{Reference page|page=196}}

===Natural===
{{See also|Marsh gas}}
In soil, methane is produced in anaerobic environments by methanogens, but is mostly consumed in aerobic zones by [[Methanotroph|methanotrophs]]. [[Methane emissions]] result when the balance favors methanogens. Wetland soils are the main natural source of methane. Other sources include oceans, forest soils, termites, and wild ruminants.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Le Mer |first1=Jean |last2=Roger |first2=Pierre |title=Production, oxidation, emission and consumption of methane by soils: A review |journal=European Journal of Soil Biology |date=January 2001 |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=25–50 |doi=10.1016/S1164-5563(01)01067-6 |bibcode=2001EJSB...37...25L |s2cid=62815957}}</ref>

===Industrial===
{{Main|Anaerobic digestion}}
'''Anaerobic digestion''' is a sequence of processes by which [[microorganisms]] break down [[biodegradable]] material in the absence of [[oxygen]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=US EPA |first=OAR |date=2019-03-18 |title=How Does Anaerobic Digestion Work? |url=https://www.epa.gov/agstar/how-does-anaerobic-digestion-work |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.epa.gov |language=en}}</ref> This process produces biogas which can be used as a fuel. Industrial biogas production can either be purpose-built such as anaerobic digesters built to process manure and organic waste or can harvest biogas produced as [[By-product|byproduct]] from [[Landfill|landfills]] or [[wastewater treatment]] plants.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=An introduction to biogas and biomethane – Outlook for biogas and biomethane: Prospects for organic growth – Analysis |url=https://www.iea.org/reports/outlook-for-biogas-and-biomethane-prospects-for-organic-growth/an-introduction-to-biogas-and-biomethane |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=IEA |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==== Biogas plants ====
A ''biogas plant'' is the name often given to an [[anaerobic digester]] that treats farm wastes, municipal organic waste and/or energy crops.<ref name=":2" /> Industrial biogas plants process organic material in an air-tight tank to create anaerobic conditions. The material is heated to either [[Mesophile|mesophilic]] (~{{convert|38|C}}) or [[Thermophile|thermophilic]] (>{{convert|55|C}}) and held for a typical retention time of two to thirty days.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 2014 |title=Anaerobic Digesters: Frequently Asked Questions |url=https://www1.agric.gov.ab.ca/$department/deptdocs.nsf/all/agdex11290/$file/768-2.pdf?OpenElement |access-date=27 October 2025 |website=Alberta Department of Agriculture}}</ref> Biogas produced from these facilities is either combusted for electricity production using a [[Cogeneration|combined heat and power]] system or [[Biogas upgrader|upgraded]] to biomethane for use in [[Natural gas vehicle|vehicles]] or natural gas distribution systems.

These plants can be fed with energy crops such as maize [[silage]] or [[Biodegradable waste|biodegradable wastes]] including sewage sludge and food waste. Feedstock type significantly influences methane yield: fats and food waste can produce up to 800 m<sup>3</sup> of gas per tonne of dry matter, while animal manure yields approximately 20-30 m<sup>3</sup> per tonne, though it offers greater process stability<ref>{{Cite web |title=Biogas Production: Understanding the Anaerobic Digestion Process - PowerUP |url=https://www.powerup.at/knowledge/biogas/how-is-biogas-produced/ |access-date=2026-07-27 |website=PowerUp – Parts for Gas-engines |language=en-US}}</ref>. During the process, the micro-organisms transform biomass waste into biogas and [[digestate]]. Higher quantities of biogas can be produced when the wastewater is co-digested with other residuals from the dairy industry, sugar industry, or brewery industry. For example, while mixing 90% of wastewater from beer factory with 10% cow whey, the production of biogas was increased by 2.5 times compared to the biogas produced by wastewater from the brewery only.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Appels|first1=Lise|last2=Baeyens|first2=Jan|last3=Degrève|first3=Jan|last4=Dewil|first4=Raf|date=2008|title=Principles and potential of the anaerobic digestion of waste-activated sludge|journal=Progress in Energy and Combustion Science|volume=34|issue=6|pages=755–781|doi=10.1016/j.pecs.2008.06.002|bibcode=2008PECS...34..755A |s2cid=95588169 |issn=0360-1285|url=https://lirias.kuleuven.be/handle/123456789/224773|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210625110047/https://lirias.kuleuven.be/handle/123456789/224773|archive-date=25 June 2021|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==== Landfill gas ====
{{Main|Landfill gas}}
[[File:Biogas_in_Indonesia_(903).jpg|thumb|An Indonesian community installs a cylindrical plastic biogas reactor in order to turn their organic waste into energy, 2007]]
Landfill gas is produced by wet organic waste decomposing under anaerobic conditions in a similar way to biogas.<ref>{{cite web |title=Biogas – Bioenergy Association of New Zealand (BANZ) |url=http://www.bioenergy.org.nz/biogas.asp |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100125053346/http://www.bioenergy.org.nz/biogas.asp |archive-date=25 January 2010 |access-date=21 February 2010 |publisher=Bioenergy.org.nz}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.epa.gov/lmop/proj/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090103070211/http://www.epa.gov/lmop/proj/|url-status=dead|title=LFG energy projects|archivedate=3 January 2009}}</ref> The waste is covered and mechanically compressed by the weight of the material that is deposited above. This material prevents oxygen exposure thus allowing anaerobic microbes to thrive. Biogas builds up and is slowly released into the atmosphere if the site has not been engineered to capture the gas. Landfill gas released in an uncontrolled way can be hazardous since it can become explosive when it escapes from the landfill and mixes with oxygen. The lower [[explosive limit]] is 5% methane and the upper is 15% methane.<ref>[http://www.adelaide.edu.au/biogas/safety/ Safety Page, Beginners Guide to Biogas] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150217044037/http://www.adelaide.edu.au/biogas/safety/|date=17 February 2015}}, www.adelaide.edu.au/biogas. Retrieved 22.10.07.</ref>

The methane in biogas is 28<ref name=":3">{{cite web |title=Archived copy |url=https://www.ipcc.ch/pdf/assessment-report/ar5/syr/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181112060025/https://www.ipcc.ch/pdf/assessment-report/ar5/syr/SYR_AR5_FINAL_full.pdf |archive-date=12 November 2018 |access-date=22 December 2018}}</ref> times more potent a greenhouse gas than carbon dioxide. Therefore, uncontained landfill gas, which escapes into the atmosphere may significantly contribute to the [[effects of global warming]]. In addition, [[Volatile organic compound|volatile organic compounds]] (VOCs) in landfill gas contribute to the formation of [[Smog#Photochemical smog|photochemical smog]].<ref name="NewSc2785p14">{{cite news |last=Gupta |first=Sujata |date=2010-11-03 |title=Cold climates no bar to biogas production |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/mg20827854.000-cold-climates-no-bar-to-biogas-production.html |newspaper=New Scientist |publisher=Sunita Harrington |location=London |page=14}}</ref>

=== Faecal sludge ===
[[Fecal sludge management|Faecal sludge]] is a product of onsite sanitation systems. After collection and transport, faecal sludge can be treated as sewage in a conventional treatment plant, or independently in a faecal sludge treatment plant. Faecal sludge can be co-treated with organic solid waste in [[Compost|composting]] or in an anaerobic digestion system that includes biogas production.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Semiyaga|first1=Swaib|last2=Okure|first2=Mackay A. E.|last3=Niwagaba|first3=Charles B.|last4=Katukiza|first4=Alex Y.|last5=Kansiime|first5=Frank|date=2015-11-01|title=Decentralized options for faecal sludge management in urban slum areas of Sub-Saharan Africa: A review of technologies, practices and end-uses|journal=Resources, Conservation and Recycling|language=en|volume=104|pages=109–119|doi=10.1016/j.resconrec.2015.09.001|issn=0921-3449|doi-access=free|bibcode=2015RCR...104..109S }}</ref> Resource Recovery and Reuse  is a subprogram of the [[CGIAR]] Research Program on Water, Land and Ecosystems. It claims post-processing for energy recovery is economically feasible and would tackle sanitation, health and environmental issues.<ref>{{Cite report |title=Testing the implementation potential of resource recovery and reuse business models: from baseline surveys to feasibility studies and business plans |last1=Otoo |first1=M. |last2=Drechsel |first2=P. |date=2016 |publisher=International Water Management Institute (IWMI). CGIAR Research Program on Water, Land and Ecosystems (WLE) |last3=Danso |first3=G. |last4=Gebrezgabher |first4=S. |last5=Rao |first5=K. |last6=Madurangi |first6=G.|doi=10.5337/2016.206 |doi-access=free |hdl=10568/75885 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

Wastewater treatment accounted for 3-4% of US electricity consumption in 2025 (vs 0.5% for electric vehicle charging. Conventional treatment processes issue ~ 21 million metric tons of greenhouse gases annually. About half of the ~15,000 [[wastewater treatment]] facilities in the USA use [[anaerobic digestion]], which typically converts <40% of the sludge into biogas. The rest typically is sent to landfills, releasing methane and CO<sub>2</sub>.

==== Dangers ====
The content of toxic [[hydrogen sulfide]] presents additional risks and has been responsible for serious accidents.<ref name="JCHAS">{{cite journal |last1=Hedlund |first1=FH |last2=Madsen|first2=M |title=Incomplete understanding of biogas chemical hazards – Serious gas poisoning accident while unloading food waste at biogas plant |journal=Journal of Chemical Health & Safety |year=2018 |volume=25 |issue=6 |pages=13–21 |doi=10.1016/j.jchas.2018.05.004|s2cid=67849856 |url=https://backend.orbit.dtu.dk/ws/files/149067495/biogas_poisioning_accident_preprint.pdf}}</ref> Leaks of unburned methane are an additional risk, because methane is a potent [[greenhouse gas]]. A facility may leak 2% of the methane.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Reinelt |first1=Torsten |last2=Liebetrau |first2=Jan |title=Monitoring and Mitigation of Methane Emissions from Pressure Relief Valves of a Biogas Plant |journal=Chemical Engineering & Technology |date=January 2020 |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=7–18 |doi=10.1002/ceat.201900180|s2cid=208716124|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Michael Fredenslund |first1=Anders |last2=Gudmundsson |first2=Einar |last3=Maria Falk |first3=Julie |last4=Scheutz |first4=Charlotte |title=The Danish national effort to minimise methane emissions from biogas plants |journal=Waste Management |date=February 2023 |volume=157 |pages=321–329 |doi=10.1016/j.wasman.2022.12.035|pmid=36592586 |bibcode=2023WaMan.157..321M|s2cid=254174784 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Biogas forms an explosive mixture with air at concentrations between approximately 6% and 22% by volume. To eliminate this hazard during maintenance, empty digesters must be properly ventilated, cleared of gas, and monitored before entry. Crucially, the system must be designed and operated to prevent negative pressure, which can draw air in and create an explosive atmosphere. This is ensured by technical controls, such as automatic shut-off devices, not merely by avoiding a specific minimum pressure.<ref>Bontempo, Giannina; Maciejczyk, Manuel; Wagner, Lucas; Findeisen, Clemens; Fischer, Mareike; Hofmann, Frank (November 2016). ''Safety first! Guidelines for the safe use of biogas technology''. Freising, Germany: German Biogas Association (Fachverband Biogas e.V.) and Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. PDF. https://www.biogas.org/fileadmin/redaktion/dokumente/medien/broschueren/safety/Safety_Guidelines_english.pdf (accessed 27 October 2023).</ref>

Frequent smell checks must be performed on a biogas system. If biogas is smelled anywhere windows and doors should be opened immediately. If there is a fire the gas should be shut off at the gate valve of the biogas system.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://werkgroepterlinden.be/Biogas.html|title=Biogas Problems|access-date=15 May 2015}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
